transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I've been dealing with really extreme mood swings for about two years and two months now. Some days I feel incredibly energetic and happy, but then I'll suddenly get extremely irritable and angry over the smallest things. It's like I'm constantly shifting between these two intense states.

During your high-energy periods, have you ever gone at least a week needing much less sleep and feeling so energized or impulsive that it caused major problems, like being hospitalized, getting into serious trouble, or losing touch with reality?

I'm not quite sure about needing less sleep, but my energy definitely overflows to the point where I can't stay still. During those times, I've done some really reckless things without thinking of the consequences, and I've even believed I had a special, grand mission in this world.

Have you ever had beliefs like having a special mission, or heard or seen things others didn’t, during a time when your mood was otherwise normal for at least 2 weeks? Or did those experiences only happen during your high-energy mood episodes?

Those beliefs about having a special mission only happen during my high-energy phases. When my mood is completely normal, I don't experience anything like that. It's only been happening during those intense episodes over the last two years and two months.

During those high-energy episodes, besides feeling you had a special mission, did you ever hear voices, see things others couldn’t, or become so convinced of unusual beliefs that others said you were out of touch with reality?

No, I have never heard voices or seen things that weren't actually there. I just strongly believed that I was a special person with a unique mission to fulfill. Other than that, I didn't have any other unusual beliefs or experiences like that.
When you believed you had a special mission, were you so certain of it that other people thought it was clearly unrealistic or bizarre, or did it feel more like an unusually strong sense of purpose?

I was absolutely convinced that I had a highly unique, special mission to save the world, and it was much more than just feeling motivated. My family and friends thought I had completely lost my mind and told me my ideas were totally unrealistic and impossible. To me, it felt like an absolute, undeniable truth at the time.

When you were convinced you had that mission, was it happening at the same time as the high energy and reckless behavior, or did that belief ever continue after your mood and energy had returned to normal?

I'm not quite sure if that belief persisted after my mood and energy went back to normal. I haven't really thought about the exact timing of when those feelings actually stopped. It's just hard to remember exactly when everything transitioned back to how it usually is.

Thinking back, after the high energy settled down, did you still believe for several days or longer that you had this special mission even though your sleep, activity, and impulsiveness were back to normal?
I'm not really sure, but I don't think I still believed in the mission after my energy levels normalized. It feels like those thoughts only stuck around while I was in that high-energy state.
During those high-energy times, about how long did the episodes usually last, and did they ever clearly last at least one full week?

Yes, those high-energy periods have definitely lasted much longer than just a week. In fact, I've been experiencing these episodes on and off, and sometimes continuously, for about two years and two months now.

During those high-energy episodes, did anyone say you were acting so differently that you seemed out of touch with reality, or did your belief about the mission mainly come across as grand but still understandable in the context of your mood?

Yes, I held a very strong belief that I had a special, important mission to fulfill. To everyone around me, this made me seem completely out of touch with reality, and they thought my ideas were impossible. However, to me, it felt absolutely real and crucial at the time.
Besides the mission belief, did you ever become disorganized, unable to care for yourself, or need emergency treatment or hospitalization because others thought you had lost touch with reality?

No, I have never been hospitalized or needed emergency treatment during those times. I've also never found myself unable to care for myself, as those specific situations haven't been part of my experience.
